model.name: Varlint — Apply & Bind Variables, Audit Tokens, Styles & Design Lint
model.description:
Varlint finds the values in your file that should be variables and are not, tells you which variable each one should be, and binds them.


YOUR IT REVIEW CAN CHECK THIS, NOT TAKE MY WORD

Varlint declares no network access, and Figma prints that on this page beside the last-updated date — so the person who approves plugins where you work can confirm it without contacting me. Your variables and your layers are already in your file; nothing about them leaves your machine, there is nothing to sign in to, and no usage is measured. There is nothing to fill in on a security questionnaire, and no service that can go down and take the plugin with it.


ALL 46 PLACES

Figma allows a variable in forty-six different places: sizes, spacing, corners, stroke weights, fill and stroke colour, every text property, effects, layout grids and component properties. Varlint looks at all of them. That number is not typed in by hand — a test reads Figma's own type definitions and fails if the two ever disagree.


IT SAYS WHICH VARIABLE

Finding a raw value is the easy half. If a variable in your file already holds that value, Varlint names it. If none does, it says so. It never offers to invent variables for you — your token set is yours.


DECISIONS, NOT ROWS

"Every padding of 16 should be spacing/md" is one decision that happens to touch thousands of layers. Varlint shows it as one row with the count on it, so a file's worth of work is a list you can actually read before you agree to it.


IT FOLLOWS YOUR FILE, NOT A RULEBOOK

Varlint reads how far your file has already got in each group — colour, spacing, corners, text — and only ticks the ones you are visibly already doing. A file that has never bound a width is not asked to start. When several variables hold the same value, the one your file already binds there wins. Nothing is guessed from variable names.


WHEN IT CAN'T, IT SAYS SO

Every binding is read back after it is written, and anything that did not take is listed with the reason: the layer is gone, the variable is gone, Figma will not allow it there. A binder that fails quietly is worse than one that fails.


FREE AND PAID

The audit is free, for ever: scan any page or the whole file, see the coverage figures, and see which variable every value should be. $5 once unlocks unlimited binding in every file you open. No subscription.

Figma Plugin: Find Replace Variables

This plugin is particularly beneficial when you have numerous variables with a similar naming structure, and you want to assign new variables by replacing parts of the variable names.


Functionality

The Find Replace Variables plugin locates and replaces variables in your Figma files. It accomplishes this by conducting a replace operation on the names of bound variables. You can do this by entering a simple string or a regex pattern.

Upon identifying the variables to be modified, the plugin will then search for variables with the new name, either locally or in any enabled library. If a match is found, it will substitute the old variable with the new one.


Usage

To use the Find Replace Variables plugin, follow these steps:

  1. Select the node(s) in your Figma file where you want to replace variables.
  2. Run the Find Replace Variables plugin with UI (Open) or in the Figma Quick Action Bar (Quick Run).
  3. Enter the string or regex pattern for the find operation.
  4. Enter the string or regex pattern for the replace operation.
  5. Run the plugin. It will replace all instances of matching variables within the selected nodes.


Example

If your variable names follow a specific structure and you often need to change multiple variables with the same naming structure, this is for you!


For example, if your variables are:

blue / 50
blue / 100
blue / 200
red / 50
red / 100
red / 200


You can change your design from blue to red by using “find and replace variables” blue → red with a single command.


Roadmap

  1. Add a preview component to the UI that checks for matching variables and replacement on the fly.


Features

  1. Supports all variable types
  2. Use normal text or regex
  3. Use UI or quick action menu

  2. Use across an unlimited number of files
  3. No subscription fees
  4. Get individual lifetime access for a one-time fee of $69 (limited time offer).


Limitations

You can’t use this on instances that have bound variables as an override.


Why not free?

Despite being a very simple plugin, it saves you a great amount of time if you really need to use it more than 3 times per file. I put a lot of effort and time into developing this plugin, while I could have done client work. model.name: Stray Component & Variable Finder (Ghost, Unindexed, Orphaned, Etc.)
model.description:
What is this plugin good for?


This plugin makes it easy to identify ‘stray’ component or variables within a design file.


What is a ‘stray' component/variable

A stray component or variable is one that either:

(1) is no longer properly linked to its original library (because the library was removed or changed), or

(2) was left behind from a previous library you no longer want to use.


Figma often identifies these in your assets panel as libraries that are ‘used in this file’ but they does not give you any indication of WHERE in the file they are being used. This plugin makes it easy to identify these components.


𖨠𖨠𖨠 If you find this plugin useful, and you feel like it, throw me some coffee dollars. 𖨠𖨠𖨠


How do I use this plugin?


1. Identify libraries you want to keep.

Start by opening the file where you want to find and fix stray components or variables. In the Assets panel, review the libraries that are currently being used in the file.


2. Index the libraries you don't want flagged as stray.

Open the plugin inside each library file you want to keep.

In the Library Manager tab, click "Index Library" for each one.

This ensures that components and variables from these libraries won't be flagged as stray later.


3. Return to your target file and run a scan.

Go back to your target file. In the plugin, open the "Scan Components/Variables" tab and choose whether you want to scan for components or variables.

The plugin will search your file for anything not included in your indexed libraries.


4. Review the results.

You'll see a list of all stray components or variables it found, along with helpful details like node names and their location in the file.





More Specific FAQ Questions 


What is the difference between Variable View and Node View for variables?


Variable View:

Organizes the scan results by each specific stray variable.

You can see all the places across your file where a particular stray variable appears.


Node View:

Organizes the scan results by the nodes that have the most stray variables.

This helps you prioritize fixing nodes with the highest number of issues, regardless of the variable types.


The scan is identifying components that belong to one of my indexed libraries as a Stray, what’s going on?


The most likely answer is that the component was deleted from the library. When this happens the component in the target file will point to its original library but does not actually exist there any longer (and therefore was not indexed)


Why can’t the plugin identify the library the stray component/variable comes from?


The Figma Plugin API does not expose data about files you own or have access to, so there is no way to get this information without adding an Authentication flow


Why can’t the plugin display the name of each variable in the results list?


Similar to the answer above, the Plugin API cannot get the name of variables from files that it does not have access to. It can only access the local name of the variable which tends to be semantically meaningless. Sorry.


Can I scan for both components and variables at the same time?


No, you’ll need to run the scan separately for components and variables. Maybe this could come in a future update.


Do I need to re-index libraries if they change?


Yes. If you update a library (e.g. delete or rename components/variables), it's a good idea to re-open that file and click “Index Library” again to make sure your scan stays accurate.


How long does the scan take?


The indexing and scanning process should be relatively quick (~3 to 30 seconds) generally; however the processing time is related to how big of a file you are scanning.

Please note, these features require a valid subscription to unlock.

Variable Rebinding


Want to switch themes?

Modes amount limit?

Use variable sets as your themes to quickly switch different variable

sets for layers, making theme switch effortless.


Follow these steps to prepare:

  1. Prepare two variable sets with different names to represent your different themes.
  2. Create a variable set `Collection A` and create a variable `background`.

Please note, `Rebind Var` cannot rebind the following attributes:

- Fill with gradient colors
- For rich text, you can only choose one of the following:
- Bind `String Variable` to Text Content
- Bind any variable to Text Style instead of the text content itself

Import and Export

  2. a-background links to Collection A - background
  3. b-background links to Collection B - background

Click the export button in the bottom right corner to generate a JSON file containing all the variable sets and variables.

Material3 Specification Templates

  3. 创建变量集 Collection B，并创建变量 background

最终你会看到图层的 Fill ，重新绑定到 Collection B - backgroud

3. 选择需要导入的变量集，对于有依赖关系的变量集，插件会自动导入依赖的变量集

4. 点击导入按钮，完成操作

Material3规范模版

model.name: Bulk Apply Variables
model.description:
Adopting Figma Variables means binding thousands of hardcoded values by hand. This plugin does it in one pass.


CATCHES WHAT EXACT MATCHING MISSES


Real files drift. The same brand blue ends up as #3B82F6, #3B82F5 and #3C82F6 after months of copy-paste and eyedropper picks. Your eye sees one color.


Plugins that compare hex strings bind the first and leave the rest behind — and those leftovers are exactly what breaks your dark mode later. This plugin compares colors the way the eye does, using CIEDE2000 perceptual distance, so all three get bound together. Tolerance is adjustable.


NOT JUST COLOR


Spacing, padding and corner radius bind to your number variables too. Numbers match exactly and never approximately — deciding that 15px "meant" 16px would silently reshape your layout.


REVIEW BEFORE ANYTHING CHANGES


Every match is grouped and listed with its occurrence count. Exact matches come pre-selected; looser matches show their perceptual distance and stay opt-in. Click any match to jump straight to it on canvas.


PRIVATE BY DESIGN


Runs entirely on your machine. No account, no network access, nothing leaves your file.


HOW TO USE


1. Open a file that already has a variable collection

2. Select layers, or choose "Entire page"

3. Scan, review the matches, Apply

model.name: Smart Pen.dev to Figma Importer with - Penport
model.description:
Import .pen designs from Pen.dev (pencil) into Figma as native nodes. Supports frames, text, vectors, components, variables, gradients, and more.

Penport bridges Pen.dev and Figma by importing `.pen` design files directly into Figma as native, editable nodes. No screenshots, no static exports — every element is a real Figma object that you can edit, restyle, and use in prototypes.


Two Import Modes


- File Mode — Drop or select a `.pen` file, browse a tree view of all nodes, check the ones you want, and import only what you need. Perfect for bringing in specific screens or components.

- Live Mode — Already working in Pencil? Copy node IDs (single or multiple), paste them into the plugin, and they get detected right away, no more searching the entire node tree!


What Gets Imported


  1. Frames: Native Figma frames with auto-layout (vertical/horizontal), padding, gap, and alignment
  2. Text: Editable text nodes with font family, weight, style, size, line height, letter spacing, and alignment
  3. Rectangles & Ellipses: Native shapes with fills, strokes, corner radius, and effects
  4. Paths (SVG): Figma Vector Networks — supports compound paths with proper evenodd winding for holes
  5. Icons: Rendered via Lucide icon font (with a colored placeholder fallback)
  6. Groups: Properly sized group frames that contain their children
  7. Gradients: Linear, radial, and angular gradients with correct rotation and color stop mapping
  8. Image fills: Local image files (drag-and-drop or folder picker) + network URLs (auto-fetched)
  9. Effects: Drop shadows, inner shadows, layer blurs, and background blurs
  10. Design Variables: Colors, strings, and numbers → Figma local variables with property bindings
  11. Reusable Components: .pen component definitions → Figma ComponentNodes + InstanceNodes with descendant overrides



Smart Auto-Layout


The plugin intelligently detects Pencil.dev's layout model and recreates it in Figma's auto-layout system:

- `layout: "horizontal" / "vertical"` → Figma auto-layout

- Frames with children infer auto layout (matching Pencil's CSS flexbox defaults)

- `layoutPosition: "absolute"` → Figma absolute positioning inside auto-layout parents

- `fill_container(NNN)` → FILL in auto-layout context, FIXED fallback size otherwise

- Padding, gap, `justifyContent`, `alignItems` — all mapped to Figma equivalents


Variable & Component Support


- Create real Figma local variables from `.pen` variable definitions (colors, strings, numbers)

- Bind variables to node properties (fill, stroke, cornerRadius, fontFamily, lineHeight, letterSpacing)

- Or decompose to static values — your choice per import

- Convert reusable `.pen` nodes into Figma ComponentNodes with `InstanceNode` references

- Descendant overrides on component instances are applied automatically

- Re-import safety: existing variable collections are reused, not duplicated


Technical Details


- File format: `.pen` (JSON-based) from Pencil.dev

- Performance: Pre-fetches network images, loads fonts before creation, creates components off-canvas

- Error handling: Graceful smart fallbacks for FILL sizing, font loading, missing images

- Progress reporting: Real-time status updates during import



## How to Use


1. Install the Lucide icon font (optional, for icon rendering):

- Download from [GitHub releases](https://github.com/lucide-icons/lucide/releases)

- Install the `.ttf` file on your system

- Restart Figma

- Enable "Use Lucide icon font" in the plugin


2. Open the plugin in Figma


3. Choose a mode:

- File Mode: Drop or click to select a `.pen` file → browse the tree → check nodes → import

- Live Mode: Select a `.pen` file first → paste node IDs from Pencil clipboard → import


4. Configure options (shown when applicable):

- Use Lucide icon font

- Import as Figma variables

- Import as Figma components


5. Click Import — your design appears in Figma as native nodes



Requirements


- Figma (desktop or web)

- A `.pen` file from Pencil.dev (https://pencil.dev)

- Lucide icon font (optional — enables icon rendering)



Support & Feedback


For issues, feature requests, or feedback, please reach out via the Figma Community page.

About


SYNCIA는 Information Architecture(IA) 데이터와 Figma를 동기화하는 자동화 플러그인입니다.

구글스프레드시트 기반 IA를 내보낸 JSON을 업로드하면,

화면 구조를 분석해 Figma 컴포넌트를 자동 생성하고 변수를 바인딩합니다.

또한 IA 변경사항을 감지해 컴포넌트를 자동 업데이트하는 워크플로우를 지원합니다.


SYNCIA is an automation plugin that syncs Information Architecture (IA) data with Figma.

Upload CSV files from Google Sheets or exported JSON from IA sheets, and the plugin analyzes screen structures to automatically generate Figma components and bind variables. It supports workflows that detect IA changes and automatically update components.


Key Features


Json Import : 구글시트에서 내보낸 Json 파일을 업로드하여 피그마 변수 체계에 맞게 화면 목록을 불러옵니다. 화면명, ID, 그룹 구조 등 모든 정보를 자동으로 파싱합니다.

Variable Sync : Figma 변수 컬렉션에서 IA 데이터를 자동으로 추출합니다. 최신 변수 컬렉션을 인식하여 화면 목록을 실시간으로 반영합니다.

Auto Component Generation : 화면 목록을 기반으로 컴포넌트를 자동 생성합니다. screen_id를 기준으로 컴포넌트명을 지정하고, 카테고리/그룹 구조를 유지합니다.

Variable Binding : 생성된 컴포넌트에 screen_id_old, screen_id, screen_name 변수를 자동 바인딩합니다. 각 컴포넌트에 해당하는 IA 데이터를 연결합니다.

Change Detection : IA 데이터의 변경사항을 감지해 추가/변경/오류 항목을 분류합니다. 변경된 변수값만 선별적으로 업데이트할 수 있습니다.

Error Validation : 변수에 "ERROR" 값이 포함된 화면을 자동으로 감지하고 별도로 표시합니다. 데이터 오류를 사전에 확인할 수 있습니다.

Category Organization : 화면을 카테고리와 그룹(SB_name, 1depth, 2depth 등)으로 자동 분류합니다. 계층 구조를 유지한 채 목록을 관리합니다.


Json Import : Upload Json files exported from Google Sheets to load screen lists. Automatically parses all information including screen names, IDs, and group structures.

Variable Sync : Automatically extracts IA data from Figma variable collections. Recognizes the latest variable collection and reflects screen lists in real time.

Auto Component Generation : Automatically generates components based on screen lists. Names components using screen_id and maintains category/group structures.

Variable Binding : Automatically binds screen_id_old, screen_id, and screen_name variables to generated components. Links IA data corresponding to each component.

Change Detection : Detects changes in IA data and categorizes them into added/changed/error items. Allows selective updates of only modified variable values.

Error Validation : Automatically detects and displays screens containing "ERROR" values in variables. Enables early verification of data errors.

Category Organization : Automatically categorizes screens by categories and groups (SB_name, 1depth, 2depth, etc.). Manages lists while maintaining hierarchical structures.
